 'Where have you been?': Karl Bushby reunites with tearful mum in Hull after 28-year journey
 2 November 2026 Radio Humberside live 
 Summary
 Karl Bushby has returned to his childhood home in Hull after leaving Chile in November 1998 with the aim of walking an unbroken path back to his roots
 To date, he has crossed four continents, swum the English Channel and walked more than 31,000 miles (58,000km)
 Family, friends and supporters have been waiting for him at the finish line
 He crossed the Humber Bridge on Sunday and was 'overwhelmed' with the reception
 The expedition has been mainly self-funded. However, sponsors have joined along the way, including a US-based documentary firm
 Karl has been sent a letter of congratulations from Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who has praised his determination and self belief
 Biju Kurian has travelled from the US to be here today. Biju says he hosted Karl for nine days when he travelled into Oklahoma in 2014
 Live Reporting
 Edited by Jen Bateman and Nathan Hemmingham. Words by Stuart Harratt
 That's all for today published at 14:47 GMT 2 November 14:47 GMT 2 November 
 Thank you for joining our live coverage of Karl Bushby's return to Hull.
 The global adventurer set off from Chile in 1998 with the aim of walking back to his childhood home.
 You can read more about it here

 Global trekker's emotional return home published at 14:39 GMT 2 November 14:39 GMT 2 November 
 Media caption, Karl Bushby reunited with his mum at home
 After 28 years away, walking 31,000-miles (50,000km), Karl Bushby has arrived at his mother's home in Hull.
 The former paratrooper set off from Chile in 1998 aged 29 and has travelled across the Bering Strait between Russia and the US, as well as swimming the English Channel.
 The 56-year-old was met by cheering crowds as he made his way from the Humber Bridge to Hull city centre, where he was met by the city's Lord Mayor for a civic reception.
 After setting off again from Hull City Hall, he walked the last few miles before an emotional reunion with his tearful mum, Angela, who joked: "Where have you been?"

 Man to get Bushby autograph tattooed published at 14:27 GMT 2 November 14:27 GMT 2 November 
 Jack Mason, 18, had his arm signed by Bushby as he approached his home. 
 He said that he was going to get it tattooed.
 “He’s inspirational," Mason said.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 What did Karl's parents think when he told them he was setting off for his trek? published at 14:14 GMT 2 November 14:14 GMT 2 November 
 Karl is now inside his childhood home, where his mum, Angela, previously told the BBC she was "gobsmacked" when Karl revealed his intention to walk home from Chile in 1998.
 The idea was supported by his father, Keith, a former SAS soldier.
 "I was gobsmacked when Karl told me what he planned to do," said Angela, a retired packer at a snack food factory who is divorced from Keith.
 "Karl has always been headstrong," she added. "Once Karl puts his mind to something, he does it."

 The world from Karl's perspective published at 13:47 GMT 2 November 13:47 GMT 2 November 
 Kevin Shoesmith 
Reporting from Hull 
 I once asked Karl if he has time to truly absorb the beauty of places he passes through, such as the stunning main square in Mons where I met him last month.
 "I'm seeing the world in a lot of detail," he said, in response to my question. "But it's from my perspective, relevant to what I'm doing.
 "And it's not like the vacation-style detail where you're going to a place to learn the culture and the food and all that kind of thing. You kind of naturally know the food of a place because you're living in it. 
 "You're certainly not spending a lot of money on a traditional dish in a fancy restaurant with them telling you this is our traditional dish. You're shoveling plates in someone's house on the side of a road somewhere, but that's their traditional stuff."
 Image caption, Karl grabs a quick photo in the centre of Mons, Belgium

 What next for Karl Bushby? published at 13:12 GMT 2 November 13:12 GMT 2 November 
 Kevin Shoesmith 
Reporting from Hull 
 I've been covering Karl's journey for 20 years. A few days ago, I joined him and fellow adventurer Angela Maxwell as they made their way north through rural Lincolnshire. 
 The key question as his journey ends will be this: what next for Karl Bushby? For years, his life has been relatively simple: get up, get from A to B, eat, sleep, repeat. The biggest hurdle may well be reintegrating into society and all the difficulties that brings.

Reporting from Hull 
 Image source, Grace McGrory / BBC French adventurer Dimitri Kieffer crossed the Bering Strait between Alaska and Russia with Karl in 2006.
 He travelled from his home in the US.
“I wanted to come here to welcome him in his home town," Kieffer said.
“It’s quite fantastic to see so much excitement in Hull about it. It’s inspirational and I have enjoyed the city.”

 'World's slowest postcard' published at 12:44 GMT 2 November 12:44 GMT 2 November 
 Months after Karl set off on his trek, he was given $100 US (£75) by Michael Bier - an Austrian ex-pat living in Chile - in return for delivering the card to a friend in Vienna.
 Michael moved to Chile from his native Austria in 1993.
 Image source, Michael Bier Earlier this year, he told the BBC : "I had earlier driven past this man who was walking along the side of a road. He was pushing a trolley containing all of his possessions.
 "I then read in a newspaper that this man was Karl Bushby and he was walking from Chile back to the UK.
 "I knew which way he was headed and I figured he would visit a general post office in order to collect his letters, so I left a little note to Karl asking him if he would deliver a postcard to my old neighbour, Dieter, when he reached Vienna."
 Days before crossing into Austria from Hungary, Karl said: "This postcard has been on a few adventurers. It's a bit ratty but it'll get to Michael's old neighbour, as promised."
 The postcard, written in German, translates to: "Dear Kerdi [a nickname]. This card was given to Karl Bushby on 7.6.1999, who is walking on foot from Punta Arenas via Bering Strait to London (sic).
 "I hope it arrives with you and you invite Karl for a few days. Greetings, Michael."
